To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sinapic acid and tocopherols are lost during oil deodorization, but the refining process generates valuable byproducts that are rich sources of these phenolics.
sinapic acid (1), sinapine, and canolol were identified in the byproducts of refining for the first time, and their antioxidant potential was confirmed.

sinapic acid, sinapine, and canolol, as well as tocopherols, were found in refining byproducts of expeller-processed canola oil, for the first-time, which indicates the value-added potential for these byproducts.

the characterization of phenolics in canola oil refining byproducts and the evaluation of their value-added potential as antioxidant-rich sources.
the characterization of phenolic compounds and tocopherols present in the byproducts of canola oil refining.
the characterization of sinapine and sinapic acid and their derivatives in canola oil refining byproducts and the evaluation of their potential as sources of natural antioxidants.

refining byproducts of expeller-processed canola oil are rich sources of sinaptic acid derivatives, tocopherols, and nonidentified phenolic antioxidants.
the byproducts of canola oil refining are rich sources of phenolic compounds and tocopherols, with antioxidant potential, and could be used for the development of value-added food ingredients.
the refining byproducts are rich sources of sinaptic acid derivatives and tocotrienols and could potentially be used as sources of natural antioxidants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the refining of expeller- pressed canola oil is not a complete loss of value-added phenolics.
the refining byproducts from expeller-pressed rapeseed and canol oil are sources of sinapoyl derivatives and tocopherol.
sinapic acid (and derivatives) and tocopherol contents of the refining byproducts are dependent on the refining method and byproduct, but all byproducts have potential as a source of antioxidants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the refining byproducts from canola oil are rich in phenolic compounds that are lost in the oil during refining.
the value-added potential for refining byproducts of canola oil is not yet fully realized.
the refining process is not as wasteful as it seems, as it generates a range of valuable byproducts.
